0.translation: Compare fixed and automatic labels on the same six source-backed pUC19 annotations. Placement, size, wrapping and device dimensions jointly affect readability; a hidden label is not a missing annotation.

2.translation: Requires optional dplyr. Original names remain in finish_features; display text merely appends actual coordinates. Intervals and strands stay fixed. All layers consume the same finish_labels, with 9 × 8 inch figures.

4.translation: ## Fixed labels: orientation, side and rotation ⟦shared:0⟧

5.translation: The feature orientation follows each feature. Each subsequent plot changes only horizontal orientation, inside placement or 30-degree rotation. Return to the common baseline instead of accumulating settings. Default overlap is hide, so crowded text may be omitted.

19.translation: | label_overlap | hide | hide/nudge/allow; allow can overlap |

20.translation: | label_rotation | NULL | Extra degrees, resolving to 0 |

22.translation: | label_circum_offset | NULL | Resolves to 0 along the circumference |

23.translation: | label_circum_limit | NULL | Resolves to TRUE for circumferential limits |

24.translation: | label_wrap | NULL | Optional character wrapping width |

25.translation: Do not pass fixed placement controls to automatic repel layers. Match the feature Position; prefer unique feature_id values for subsets/reordering and never reuse an ID for a different interval. In linear mode radial/tangent mean vertical/horizontal rather than circular letter placement.

26.translation: ## Compare four automatic layouts on identical text ⟦shared:0⟧

27.translation: Default feature first tries internal, then adjacent/external placement. Radial, auto and callout provide alternative placement strategies. Layout changes presentation, not source annotations. Keep identical text, requested size and dimensions across all four.

37.translation: Starting from feature, change only label_fit to shrink; then return to baseline and set only label_wrap=14. Shrink explicitly permits smaller text down to the default minimum 1.5. It does not shrink indefinitely to guarantee all names. Character wrapping width is not a fixed physical width.

42.translation: From the 14-character wrap example, change only label_fit to ellipsis. Then return to default feature placement and disable only external fallback. Omission/hiding changes display, not source names or features.

50.translation: | label_layout | feature | feature/radial/auto/callout; gene layouts differ |

51.translation: | label_fit | wrap | wrap/none/ellipsis/auto/shrink; omission does not edit source text |

55.translation: | external | TRUE | FALSE prevents exterior fallback; linear mode rejects this constraint |

56.translation: | max_overlaps | Inf | Does not guarantee zero collisions |

57.translation: | label_segment_overlap | fade | Appearance of conflicting leaders |

59.translation: | label_segment_linetype | auto | Automatic leader line type |

60.translation: | label_segment_layer | below | below/above; text retains the label layer position |

61.translation: | label_repeat | individual | bracket shares a counted label and arc bracket for consecutive matching short features |

62.translation: | label_segment_colour | auto | Grey for leaders from inside features to exterior labels; accepts an explicit colour |

63.translation: Read exported label placement and fit diagnostics before changing dimensions, label subsets, layout or wrapping. Keep original full names rather than retaining only truncated figure text.

64.translation:
Feature layout uses direct leaders, allowing them to cross features without
multi-bend detours. Filled features cover leaders drawn below; transparent
fills keep their transparency. Internal single-line names follow circular
tracks. Wrapped sources keep one annotation and a continuous glyph on closed
circles; a visible coordinate gap retains separate display pieces. A shifted adjacent name receives a short attachment. To restore the
label layer's drawing order:

67.translation: Change only label_max_lines to 3 and explain any improvement. At fixed dimensions, compare exterior fallback on/off. Fixed and automatic layers have different controls. Supply explicit label text or anno, checking IDs, intervals, strands and unique feature_id values. Continue with [primer text](⟦shared:0⟧) and the [dense pETDuet-1 case](⟦shared:1⟧).

68.translation:
Neighbouring names compare radial travel with angular displacement; an empty
inner track can preserve association better than squeezing names onto the
nearest track. Dotted arrow boundaries can come from source segments or
cleavage markers. Inspect ⟦shared:0⟧, ⟦shared:1⟧ and ⟦shared:2⟧;
a boundary is not necessarily an independent feature. Top-level feature
labels do not automatically add text for every named subsegment.

69.translation:
Dense inner annotations retain source-angle order. Candidate slots check
text and leaders together. Leaders may cross features, but do not acquire
multi-bend detours around text. With external placement enabled, compact
repeated annotations in outer bands can use the exterior queue as a group;
inner bands first try inner slots before exterior fallback. This bounded
search does not guarantee every density fits inside; inspect visibility,
convergence and conflict diagnostics at export dimensions.

71.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ is an explicit display style; the default
⟦shared:1⟧ retains separate labels. Consecutive non-overlapping short
features in one band can share a counted arc label and range bracket when
name, type, direction and resolved fill agree. An intervening annotation
breaks the run. Arrows, coordinates and biological rows remain independent.
Visibility and fit exports report ⟦shared:2⟧ for the shared
sources. This applies to the ⟦shared:3⟧ layout on a single closed circular
sequence; other coordinates retain individual labels. The curved range marker
is distinct from the label's simple leader.

73.translation:
Automatic plasmid axis text hugs the backbone; explicit offsets keep their
placement. Circular feature bands reserve gutters for names that cannot fit
inside their arrows, and text tracks use measured heights and physical gaps.
Explicit ⟦shared:0⟧ remains a minimum. This bounded search does not guarantee
conflict-free placement at every density; inspect actual-size export diagnostics.

74.translation:
Default grey dashed lines connect **a feature inside the sequence circle to
an exterior feature label**. Internal neighbouring labels and restriction
leaders retain their established style. A centred, isolated name close to its
feature omits an unnecessary short attachment; displaced or competing names
retain association leaders.

76.translation:
Explicit parameters affect all feature leaders in the layer. A custom
⟦shared:0⟧ theme also overrides the automatic palette.
Segment boundaries clip to the actual arrow contour without editing source
segments. Wrapped internal labels use a separate concentric baseline for each
line. Automatic coordinate text retains a small physical backbone gap;
explicit offsets keep their contract.

77.translation:
Automatic coordinate text searches only a bounded channel near the backbone.
With ⟦shared:0⟧ enabled, an unavailable nearby slot may hide
ordinary intermediate text while retaining its tick. Origin/end and combined
seam strings take priority and remain visible. Diagnostics report ⟦shared:1⟧ and
keep the original value in ⟦shared:2⟧. Hidden text uses an empty display
string so missing-value markers cannot appear as literal “NA”.

78.translation:
Unresolved endpoint clearance reports ⟦shared:0⟧ while retaining
its text. External feature leaders also honour ⟦shared:1⟧:
fade reduces opacity under text, clip removes covered portions, and show
keeps the full route. Clipping splits existing legs without adding bends.
